stories.headline: Two dead, three injured in suspected fentanyl-laced overdose at Aurora apartment
stories.summary:
Two people died and three others were hospitalized after a suspected fentanyl-laced drug overdose at an Aurora apartment complex early Monday. The incident occurred on East 16th Avenue near Kingston Street. Police responded after receiving a report of an unconscious person in one of the units.

Officers found multiple people suffering apparent overdose symptoms. A man and a woman were pronounced dead at the scene. Three other adults were taken to hospitals for poisoning and were listed as stable, though their conditions were not immediately known.

The Drug Enforcement Administration's Rocky Mountain Field Division said it was aware of the incident. The agency said that, to its knowledge, it is the largest overdose or poisoning case in its division, which covers Colorado, Utah, Wyoming and Montana, since February 2022, when five adults died of accidental fentanyl poisoning in Commerce City. An Aurora police official said the case remains active and ongoing.

stories.headline: Aurora municipal court refusing to appoint lawyers for low-income defendants, groups allege
stories.summary:
The ACLU of Colorado and the Colorado Freedom Fund allege that Aurora's municipal court is not providing attorneys to low-income defendants, despite a new state law requiring it. In an Oct. 1 letter to city leaders, the groups asked Aurora to take expeditious action to comply. They said many indigent defendants are being left to handle complex cases alone.

Gov. Jared Polis signed House Bill 1134, the Fairness & Transparency in Municipal Court Act, in April. It clarifies that municipal court defendants have a right to counsel when an offense carries the possibility of jail time. That right already exists in state court.

At an Oct. 8 hearing, Presiding Judge Shawn Day said he was not following the law because he viewed it as an unfunded mandate. The city waived jail in the case before him that day. City spokesperson Joe Rubino said the judge found the bill's requirements go beyond what is constitutionally required, and declined further comment because the case could be appealed. The groups say counsel must be provided whenever the city code permits incarceration, whether or not prosecutors seek jail.

stories.headline: Denver police officer fired after review of burglary alarm response before fatal house fire
stories.summary:
A Denver police officer has been fired after an internal investigation concluded he did not properly investigate a burglary alarm at a home where an elderly couple died in a fire shortly afterward. FOX31 Denver reported the findings. The termination closes a department review of how the alarm call was handled.

The review centered on the officer's response to the call and found that the check of the property fell short of what was required. That finding was the basis for the firing.

Few other details have been made public. The officer's identity, the home's address and the circumstances of the fire have not been disclosed. Denver officers can appeal discipline to the Civil Service Commission, and the Office of the Independent Monitor oversees the department's disciplinary system. It is not clear whether an appeal has been filed.

stories.headline: Missing Denver-area hiker found dead after fall on Humboldt Peak
stories.summary:
Search crews found the body of a missing 31-year-old hiker from the Denver metro area on Humboldt Peak, a southern Colorado 14er, on Tuesday. The Colorado Army National Guard located evidence of a fatal fall on the north side of the mountain just before 1 p.m.

The man was described as an experienced hiker. Custer County Search and Rescue announced the recovery in a press release around 4 p.m. Nov. 24.

The death comes as early winter conditions affect Colorado's high peaks, where snow and ice can make routes hazardous.

stories.headline: Mild, dry weather expected through Thanksgiving as flurries pass over Denver
stories.summary:
A weak weather system brought a few flurries to the Denver metro area overnight, but no accumulation was expected in the city. The mountains saw heavier snow showers, with rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour possible. A Winter Weather Advisory covered the central and southern mountains, with 2 to 4 inches expected along the I-70 corridor.

A ridge of high pressure will bring drier, warmer conditions for Thanksgiving travel. Highs across the Front Range and eastern plains should reach the upper 40s and low 50s Tuesday and Wednesday. Thanksgiving is forecast to be mostly sunny with highs in the mid to upper 50s, and some Denver neighborhoods could top 60 on Friday.

Another storm arrives from the northwest Friday and Saturday, bringing more mountain snow. Forecasters are still working out whether the Denver metro will see any precipitation. Denver has yet to record its first measurable snowfall of the season.

stories.headline: RTD launches webpage to help visitors plan Boulder trips for Sundance Film Festival
stories.summary:
The Regional Transportation District has launched a web landing page to help people plan trips to the 2027 Sundance Film Festival, which runs Jan. 21-31 in Boulder. The page collects service information, route details and trip-planning resources for attendees, staff, volunteers and Boulder residents.

Boulder-area routes including BOLT, JUMP, SKIP, CHAT and the city-provided HOP will operate as free-fare routes during the festival. CHAT is a temporary route providing access to Chautauqua Park, a key venue. Regional connections such as SkyRide routes AB and AL and the Flatiron Flyer will run with regular fares, extended hours and additional vehicles.

The page also points riders to the NextRide app for real-time schedules, Park-n-Ride information and a security reporting section, along with winter safety reminders. RTD is the festival's transit partner for its first year in Boulder.

stories.headline: Man with ponytail accused of throwing eggs at Waymo vehicles in Denver more than 30 times
stories.summary:
A man with a ponytail and beard has trapped Waymo self-driving taxis in Denver and thrown eggs at them more than 30 times, according to a Denver Police Department report. The account was first reported by 9News.

Since Waymo launched to the public in Denver, 9News has reported a series of incidents involving the vehicles. They have passed barricades at farmers markets, nearly driven over a freshly paved road near Sloan's Lake and received a parking citation.

The report adds to public scrutiny of the autonomous taxi service as it expands in the city.

stories.headline: Colorado's four new members of Congress cite affordability and accountability as priorities
stories.summary:
Colorado's four incoming U.S. representatives say they are eager to begin work when they are sworn in Jan. 3, after attending new-member orientation in Washington. Orientation covered ethics and disclosure rules, committee assignments and staff hiring.

The delegation includes Melat Kiros, a Denver Democrat who will represent the 1st District, and Eileen Laubacher, a Highlands Ranch Democrat and former Navy rear admiral who unseated Rep. Lauren Boebert in the 4th District. Manny Rutinel, a Commerce City Democrat, defeated Rep. Gabe Evans in the 8th District. Jessica Killin, a Colorado Springs Democrat and former congressional staffer, flipped the 5th District, becoming its first Democratic representative.

The members said affordability and accountability will be focal points of their work.

stories.headline: Polis reflects on eight years in office as Weiser prepares to take over
stories.summary:
Gov. Jared Polis told KKTV 11 News he is proud of the state's progress on education, citing universal full-day kindergarten, universal preschool now in its third year, and a high school graduation rate that rose from 80.4% to 85.6%. He also pointed to the closure of the Drake Power Plant in Colorado Springs and progress on clean energy.

On health care, Polis cited the cap on insulin costs, a viable individual insurance exchange and greater billing transparency. He said housing work remains unfinished and called for shorter approval times and less paperwork to build more homes.

Polis said he plans to spend time with family, focus on education, including second-language instruction beginning in early grades, and explore business opportunities. Governor-elect Phil Weiser, Polis's attorney general, will be sworn in Jan. 12.

stories.headline: Kelly Whitaker to open bakery and wine bar in former Port Side space in Five Points
stories.summary:
Chef and restaurateur Kelly Whitaker, behind the two-Michelin-star Wolf's Tailor, will reopen the shipping containers that housed Port Side at 2500 Larimer St. as part of his Id Est group. The 900-square-foot space will serve as a Dry Storage bakery cafe from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. and convert to a 20-seat wine bar called SomeSuch at 5 p.m. Both are expected to open in January.

Property owner Gravitas Development Group approached Whitaker after Port Side's owner closed the coffee shop over the summer. Whitaker is working with Wolf's Tailor chef Taylor Stark and Mike Capoferri of Semiprecious on the menu and bar. SomeSuch will pour only North American wines.

Dry Storage began in Boulder to use grain Whitaker grew and milled. Its mill will move to a larger facility to supply both bakeries and restaurant customers.

stories.headline: In-N-Out and Dutch Bros file site plans for new Denver locations
stories.summary:
In-N-Out Burger and Dutch Bros Coffee have filed site plans for new Denver locations, according to the Denver Business Journal. The filings follow concept approvals for projects on 56th Avenue and Leetsdale Drive.

The site plan stage is a further step in the city's development review process. It signals that both chains are moving toward expanding their presence in the city.

Further approvals would be needed before construction begins.

stories.headline: Avalanche's Cale Makar hopes to return Wednesday after three-game absence
stories.summary:
Colorado Avalanche defenseman Cale Makar said he hopes to return to the lineup Wednesday after missing three games with a lower-body injury. He said he is ready to take over a little bit upon his return.

Makar's potential return comes as the team deals with significant injuries. Forward Nathan MacKinnon is now expected to miss about 12 weeks.

Colorado recently beat the Anaheim Ducks 4-0, with goaltender Scott Wedgewood earning his first shutout of the season.

topStory.headline: Times Now Live Blog Offers Rolling Coverage of Day's Top News, but Source Contains No Specific Story Details
topStory.summary:
The source material provided for this report is a landing-page description for the Times Now Digital Breaking News Live Blog, not an article about a specific event. It states that the blog offers real-time updates on politics, business and the economy, national and international affairs, and other major developments from India and around the world. No individual news event, date, location, official statement or data point is included in the text.

Because the source names no people, institutions, governments or incidents, it is not possible to say who is involved in the day's top story, what was said or done, or what took place. Any account of a specific event would require information that is not present in the material supplied, and 303 News does not publish claims it cannot attribute to a source.

Times Now Digital is the online arm of Times Now, an Indian English-language news network, and its live blogs typically aggregate headlines as they develop through the day. Such pages are updated continuously, so the content visible at any given moment reflects a changing set of stories rather than a single fixed report. The description provided gives no indication of which stories were leading at the time of publication.

Readers seeking details on the day's major developments should consult the live blog directly or other reporting with specific, attributable content. This summary will be updated if a source describing a particular event, with named participants, verifiable facts and context, becomes available.
